title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
summary: AI agents can now use Ollama's cloud models safely inside Fly.io's cloud computers.
body_markdown:
Ollama Cloud now works inside full Linux computers designed for agents using[Fly.io](https://fly.io/) Sprites.


A[Sprite](https://sprites.dev/) is a sandbox from Fly.io. Each one is a full Linux virtual machine with its own disk that stays around between sessions. Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI are supported out of the box and will let agents run in a sandbox to securely run commands.


With the new Ollama Connector, your Sprites can use Ollama’s cloud models like kimi-k3, glm-5.3 and deepseek-v4.1-flash.


## How it works


You add your Ollama API key to your Fly.io organization, and Fly.io encrypts it and never returns it through the API.


When code inside a Sprite calls Ollama, it goes through a Fly.io gateway. The gateway checks which Sprite is calling and adds your key to the request. The Sprite itself only knows a gateway URL and a connection ID.


This means:


- An agent in a Sprite can’t leak your key.
- New connectors block every Sprite by default. You choose which ones get access: by label, by name prefix or all of them.
- Calls only work from inside a Sprite.


## Get started


You’ll need an[Ollama API key](https://ollama.com/settings/keys) and at least one Sprite.


1. In the[Fly.io dashboard](https://fly.io/dashboard) , open **Sprites** , then **Connectors** , and add an **Ollama** connector with your API key.
2. Under **Access Configuration** , choose which Sprites can use it and save.
3. Click **Test reachability** next to a Sprite to check that it can reach Ollama.


Then, from inside the Sprite:


```text
curl "https://api.sprites.dev/v1/gateway/ollama/<connection_id>/v1/chat/completions" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"model": "kimi-k3", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'


```


The connector page shows this command with your connection ID filled in. There’s no` Authorization` header because the gateway adds your key.


### Python


Any OpenAI SDK works. Set` base_url` to the gateway and use any value for` api_key` :


```text
from openai import OpenAI


client = OpenAI(
base_url="https://api.sprites.dev/v1/gateway/ollama/<connection_id>/v1",
api_key="unused",
)


response = client.chat.completions.create(
model="glm-5.3",
messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Why is the sky blue?"}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)


```


Ollama’s native` /api/*` routes work through the gateway too.


### Coding agents


Fly.io Sprites come with a skill that tells Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI about Ollama. If the Sprite has access, the agent can use Ollama models without any setup.


## Example: fuzzing


Fly.io has a guide that uses several models together. A small model like nemotron-3-nano:30b writes malformed inputs, a Sprite runs them against your program, and a larger model like kimi-k3 looks at the crashes. To switch models, change the` model` field. See the[Ollama Connector quickstart](https://sprites.dev/) .


Thank you to the Fly.io team for building this with us.
